lines.trans: Hey mister, I can't believe you take gigs like this. Why don't you be a little pickier about your work?
Because I have a family to support, I gladly take on any job at all.
Sorry, everyone—today's shoot just got canceled, so you're free to head home.

words.gram: colloquial variant of すみません
Past た-form of なる (to become).
て-form of 帰る (go/come home), used here as a gentle request.
Na-adjective used here for a polite refusal.

lines.trans: A producer ran off with the money, so we can't even pay for today's studio.
Young lady, shall we get ready and head out?
If people on the street could see right through my briefs, it would trouble them—call it basic etiquette.
We already have a studio! All we have to do is shoot right out here!
Do you want to become a director someday? You're still missing one thing: a stack of criminal convictions!
If we shoot out here, there's no studio fee—it's completely free!
That's not the issue—we're going to get arrested! Ugh, fine, I got the camera!
Here we go—ready, action! Film the actress's face, not mine!
Yes, I am Toru Muranishi! Whenever you feel like dying, look down—I'm right down here!

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

examples.text: 選んでくださり、ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for selecting me.

examples.text: あら、じゃあわたくしのも選んでいただこうかしら。広告のお仕事がありますの。
examples.trans: Oh my, then perhaps I'll ask you to pick something for me too. I have an ad shoot coming up.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Standard word for family.

examples.text: 週末は家族と過ごします。
examples.trans: I spend weekends with my family.
Everyone in my family is doing well.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun.

examples.text: 分からないことがあれば何でも聞いてください。
examples.trans: If there's anything you don't understand, ask anything.

examples.text: 彼は料理なら何でも作れる。
examples.trans: He can make anything when it comes to cooking.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of もらう; volitional いただこう means 'let's take them / I'll have them'.

forms.title: Key forms of いただく

examples.text: お時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you spare me some time?

meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.

examples.text: すいません、今日ちょっと中止になったんで、もう帰ってもらって結構っす。
examples.trans: Sorry, everyone—today's shoot just got canceled, so you're free to head home.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.en: go home; leave and go back
meanings.note: Repeated past form 帰った、帰った! is an idiomatic shooing command ('off you go, go on home!').
After なくて (隠さなくて結構です), politely says 'there is no need to'.

examples.text: 明日は来なくて結構です。
examples.trans: You do not need to come tomorrow.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Refers to humans in general or human nature.

examples.text: 人間には表と裏がある。
examples.trans: Human beings have a public face and a hidden side.

meanings.note: Godan verb; 持ってくる means 'bring'.

examples.text: 制作の人間が金持って逃げちゃったんで、今日のスタジオ代も払えません。
examples.trans: A producer ran off with the money, so we can't even pay for today's studio.

examples.text: ここで撮ればね、スタジオ代かかりませんから。タダですからね。
examples.trans: If we shoot out here, there's no studio fee—it's completely free!

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: 金さえ払えば、村西さんは釈放される。
examples.trans: As long as we pay the money, Muranishi will be released.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

examples.text: これね、透けるとね街ゆく皆様にご迷惑がかかりますからね。少しでもね、エチケット。
examples.trans: If people on the street could see right through my briefs, it would trouble them—call it basic etiquette.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 白、黒、黄色、あらゆる人種、あらゆる性癖。
examples.trans: White, Black, Asian—every race and every desire!

examples.text: これね、透けるとね街ゆく皆様にご迷惑がかかりますからね。少しでもね、エチケット。
examples.trans: If people on the street could see right through my briefs, it would trouble them—call it basic etiquette.

meanings.note: Polite/honorific plural pronoun for addressing an audience or group.

examples.text: 皆様のご健康をお祈りします。
お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

examples.text: これね、透けるとね街ゆく皆様にご迷惑がかかりますからね。少しでもね、エチケット。
examples.trans: If people on the street could see right through my briefs, it would trouble them—call it basic etiquette.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。
近い将来爆発的に普及する衛星放送についてご存じですか？
examples.trans: Have you heard of satellite broadcasting, which will soon spread explosively?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Native Japanese counter for general objects and abstract things like reasons.

examples.text: 理由がもう一つあります。
りんごを一つください。

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').

examples.text: 数もいいんですけど、もっと看板になるような作品も作らないと。
examples.trans: Volume is fine, yet we also need to make a true flagship film.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.
Used for social/work issues as well as test questions.

examples.text: それは大きな問題です。
特に問題はありません。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: 覚えてるかな？村西さんがハワイで捕まった時のこと。
examples.trans: Do you remember when Mr. Muranishi was arrested overseas?

examples.text: いやそういう問題じゃねえ、捕まるぞおい！分かったよ！
examples.trans: That's not the issue—we're going to get arrested! Ugh, fine, I got the camera!

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Formal/polite transition; contracts to それじゃ or じゃあ in casual speech.

examples.text: それでは始めましょう。

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 行く and 来る.

examples.text: それでは参りましょう。

meanings.note: Film/theater cue or general noun from English 'action'.

examples.text: 次のアクションを起こす。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Standard polite 'goodbye'.
